name: Blastus
source_summary: Herod Agrippa I's personal chamberlain, whose favor the people of Tyre and Sidon won in order to negotiate peace with the king, shortly before Herod's public, fatal act of pride.
family_friendly_summary: Blastus worked closely with King Herod Agrippa as his personal assistant, trusted with access to the king. Herod was angry with the cities of Tyre and Sidon, and they depended on Herod's country for their food, so they needed to make peace with him. To get an audience with the king, the people of Tyre and Sidon first won Blastus over to their side, since he could help arrange a meeting. Soon after peace was made, Herod gave a public speech, and the people flattered him by shouting that he sounded like a god. Because Herod accepted the praise instead of giving glory to God, he was suddenly struck down and died.
adult_story: Blastus was the personal chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I, a trusted household official with access to the king. When Herod, angry with the cities of Tyre and Sidon, threatened them, their leaders sought peace, since their region depended on food supplied from Herod's territory (Acts 12:20). To gain an audience with the king, they first won Blastus to their side -- his favor was the door into Herod's presence. Blastus is mentioned only this once, a minor courtier at the edge of a much larger event: shortly after this peace was secured, Herod appeared before the assembled crowd in royal robes and delivered a public address. The people flattered him, shouting, "The voice of a god and not of a man!" Because Herod accepted their worship instead of giving God the glory, an angel of the Lord struck him down immediately, and he died, eaten by worms (12:21-23). Blastus's small, practical role in brokering political favor sits right beside one of Scripture's starkest warnings about a ruler who let others praise him as divine.
